extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians and comedy writers studying joke craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for constructing and editing stand-up joke material in the style of John Mulaney, emphasizing image precision, word choice, sentence rhythm, performer persona, road-testing, and callback architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joke in precision of image (not just punchline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the joke in PRECISION of image, not just in punchline?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a clear, fully formed image (e.g., a child sitting still in a restaurant). Walk the audience through that image with PRECISION. The joke lives in the precise framing rather than any single line. The punchline often re-frames what kind of image the audience has been looking at.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funny specific noun choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you chosen the funny specific noun, not the generic one?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the funny noun, not the cool one. Concrete, specific, slightly outdated proper nouns are preferred (examples: 'Quiznos' is funnier than 'sandwich shop'; 'Diane' is funnier than 'my friend'). Pick particular, image-rich nouns over generic descriptors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentence rhythm: luxuriate then contract
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the sentence luxuriate before it contracts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mulaney's signature is the long, baroque sentence with a sudden plain ending. Let the setup luxuriate; let the punch contract. The rhythmic deflation itself functions as the joke: extended, ornate lead-in followed by a stark, simple landing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persona: discovering with the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the persona discovering with the audience, not lecturing them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a discovery-tone — the precocious-child-explaining-adulthood persona — so it feels like the performer is discovering absurdity in real time alongside the audience. This earns attention and allows the performer to be clever without alienating listeners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and edit via road-testing and cutting
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you tested it in 50+ rooms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop bits live (often for ~two years) and use road-testing to decide what survives. Final recorded/produced versions typically cut roughly 30% from the road version. Material that lands in many rooms (e.g., 50+) is what should be preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Callbacks as architecture, not signposts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design callbacks to pay off 10–15 minutes later; don't overtly signal them. The audience should not see the seed — they should discover the payoff — making the show reward re-watching and feel architected rather than obviously stitched together.
